---
title: "Amendment 001: same-month deaths with zero released follow-up"
subtitle: "Post-freeze amendment before association modelling, 16 September 2026"
format: html
---

## Status

Prospective amendment to protocol and SAP version 0.3. It was written after the
mortality fields were opened, but before any exposure-outcome association model
was fitted.

## Trigger

The frozen SAP specified elapsed months from the MEC examination as the primary
time scale, using `PERMTH_EXM` from the 2019 public-use linked mortality files.
During cohort construction, four eligible participants had `PERMTH_EXM = 0` and
`MORTSTAT = 1`. These observations were distributed across the 2001–2002,
2003–2004 and 2007–2008 cycles. No censored participant had zero follow-up.

The combination indicates a death recorded in the same monthly interval as the
MEC examination. It is not compatible with a Cox model if represented as an
event at exactly zero elapsed time.

## Decision

For these four records only, the primary analysis will assign 0.5 months of
follow-up, the midpoint of the first monthly interval. The released value will
remain unchanged in `follow_up_months_released`; the analysis value will be
stored separately in `follow_up_months`; and `zero_follow_up_death` will identify
the affected records.

The cohort-building script must verify that exactly four zero-month records are
present and that all four are deaths. Any different count or any zero-month
censored record will stop the pipeline.

## Sensitivity analysis

A sensitivity analysis will refit the primary model after excluding the four
same-month deaths. This will assess whether the midpoint convention materially
affects the estimated CRP association.

## Rationale

The exact event day is unavailable in the public-use file. Assigning the midpoint
of the known monthly interval preserves the observed deaths, produces a positive
analysis time and makes the approximation explicit. Exclusion is not used in the
primary analysis because it would discard observed outcome events solely because
their public follow-up time is grouped to months.

## Classification

This is an outcome-informed, post-freeze implementation amendment. It does not
change the exposure, outcome definition, eligible population, covariates,
estimand or primary model. It resolves a time-coding condition that could not be
quantified during the pre-outcome audits.
